rubric_notes: All must_include met: a.22.1 (47113) superfamily with families a.22.1.1/47114, a.22.1.2/47129, a.22.1.3/47134, a.22.1.4/101318 in SCOPe 2.08; superfamily = probable common ancestry; family distinctions preserved and function transfer (nucleosome assembly, SOS signaling) explicitly rejected. Fold/class caveats correct; linker histone a.4.5.13 (46827) in a.4.5/a.4 correct; H-NS/HU 'histone-like' naming caveat. All identifiers and members match evidence bundle. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct families a.204.1.2/a.204.1.4, superfamily a.204.1 (101386) with homology record, domain SUNIDs and A:7-93 boundary all match evidence. Distinguishes superfamily homology from fold/class similarity, cites five-helix active-site module, names hypothetical Sulfolobus protein vs M. tuberculosis HisE, and explicitly rejects HisE/MazG function transfer in both directions with required external evidence named. No material issues.

Correctly places c.55.1.1, c.55.1.3, c.55.1.4 within c.55.1 (SUNID 53067, supported by children endpoint), with fold c.55 and class c. Infers remote common ancestry and a conserved nucleotide-binding catalytic framework; explicitly distinguishes fold-level similarity from homology. Rejects transfer of substrate specificity, catalytic mechanism, cellular role, and whole-protein architecture; names external evidence needed. Regulation and oligomeric state are not named explicitly but the function-transfer limit is clearly stated. No factual errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers for release 2.08; superfamily children, bimetal-ion-centre annotation, and the RNR-like family's desaturase/monooxygenase members are supported by the cited children and annotation endpoints. States superfamily expresses probable relatedness stronger than fold alone and that family membership does not guarantee identical chemistry; frames different functions as diversification of a binuclear-metal helical scaffold. Rejects transfer of metal specificity, substrate, mechanism, radical chemistry, assembly, and active-site templating; requires sequence/profile evidence, ligand-residue comparison, experimental metal occupancy and activity, and partner/assembly information. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete hierarchy with correct SCCS and SUNIDs verified against bundle (including class 48724 and fold description '7 strands in 2 sheets, greek-key'). States superfamily implies probable common ancestry without implying identical function. Cites family annotations 'lacking the metal-binding site' (in bundle). Rejects copper/electron-transfer transfer and names required evidence (coordinating residue geometry, copper occupancy, redox assays). Correctly notes PAD4 N-terminal domain classification does not carry catalytic activity. No violations.

Correct families, SUNIDs, superfamily, fold, class (53931), release 2.08; all in bundle. States superfamily expresses probable common ancestry while fold/class alone does not. Rejects annotating UBX/RBD as covalent modifiers, assigning ubiquitination/proteasomal targeting superfamily-wide, and transferring Ras- or p97-binding across families; caveats ubiquitin-related family; names required evidence and limits of template use. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct three families under c.23.1 (52172) with SUNIDs, fold c.23, class c; children listing in bundle confirms. States superfamily is stronger evidence than fold/class and does not make the domains one interchangeable family. Rejects phosphorylation competence, kinase partners, chemotaxis, decarboxylation/PLP, and circadian role; treats wing as accessory domain, not catalytic unit; quotes supported KaiA annotation. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct superfamily/family/fold/class with SUNIDs and fold comment; V1 and A1 bulge domains in the family supported by search results; siblings named. Treats hierarchy as graded evolutionary hypothesis, states separation means insufficient evidence to unite rather than proof of independent origin, distinguishes family from superfamily, rejects function transfer. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Identifiers and hierarchy correct; clear same-fold-versus-same-superfamily argument; avoids both must_avoid traps; evidence list covers sequence/profile, structure, heme ligation and evolutionary evidence. Does not use the f.21.3 possible-link or superfamily comments available in SCOPe, so the calibrated-uncertainty discussion is thinner than the fuller answers. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct SCCS/SUNIDs for families, superfamily, fold, class; release 2.08 confirmed via /releases/current. Level semantics explained correctly (family closer, superfamily probable remote homology, fold/class not sufficient, no branching order). Succinyl-CoA synthetase example and c.2.1.8-vs-other-CoA-binders distinction supported by search results. Refuses ADH/CoA/NAD(P)/channel-regulation transfer; domain vs whole-protein; evidence requirements listed. No material issues.

Names shared family k.40.1.1 Designed trimeric coiled-coil (SUNID 100905), quotes the 'not a true family' annotation, states the caveat overrides ordinary family-level inference and the generic homology_implied_by_level flag, describes the pair as a designed structural grouping without established ancestry, and rejects function/amyloidogenicity transfer. All SUNIDs, SCCS, and the comment are supported by the bundle. No unmet criteria. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Concise but complete. 1.69: d1t1ja_ own fold c.137/c.137.1/c.137.1.1, d1f8ya_ in c.23/c.23.14/c.23.14.1; 2.08: d1t1ja1 in c.23.14.2, same superfamily c.23.14 (renamed N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like), families kept distinct. Interprets change as recognition of evolutionary relationship at superfamily level, merging previously separate fold/superfamily placements. Rejects function transfer. All identifiers supported by bundle parents calls. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Complete: synthetic N-terminal tag H:1-8 SUNID 343393, l.1.1.1 in class l Artifacts with Tags at all levels; d1a14h1 H:9-111 VH domain b.1.1.1/b.1.1/b.1/b with level names; tag similarity not homology evidence, exclude/mask, no function transfer or template use; fold/class alone does not establish ancestry. All identifiers and hierarchy match the bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly contrasts the single whole-chain d1acca_ (f.11.1.1) with the 2.08 pair d1acca2 A:14-225 (b.179.1.1, PA14) and d1acca1 A:226-735 (f.60.1.1), including SUNIDs and class moves. Good modular-evolution reasoning: rejects whole-chain transfer from a PA14-only hit, rejects fold-alone homology, and warns against remapping legacy hits. Does not identify 2.04 as the release where the split appears, giving only a 'by 2.08' statement, so the required before/after release comparison is imprecise. Also omits that the C-terminal unit still spans structural domains II-IV, so the reader could misread the split as exhausting the chain's subdivisions.

All identifiers, boundaries, and classifications correct and supported; mosaic interpretation with reused modules vs new fold d.394; notes class e multidomain nature of RT unit; appropriate caveats on homology level, function transfer, and new-fold meaning. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete answer: lengths 51/373/752 identified as construct lengths, repeat count and boundaries as the source of variation, shared family a.298.1.1 within a.298.1 / a.298 / class a, and explicit use of the 'single repeat' comment and the 're' repeat-related exception on two domains plus the 34-residue representative 4cj9 A:259-292 that applies only to that representative. States that family and superfamily convey relatedness while fold and class do not, and refuses DNA-specificity and array-template transfer.

Release metadata (2.08, 2.08-stable, dates, 2.08-2026-08-16) is correct and bundle-supported. Citation guidance correct: 2.08-stable or the exact dated identifier, not 'current'/'latest'. Correctly says the periodic label is not a new stable release. However it never states what the periodic update contains, i.e. that it adds newly classified PDB entries without rewriting older stable-release domains; the semantics are given only in the negative. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete and explicit: shared a.47.2.1 placement with all SIDs, fragment/ms annotations vs four-long-helix bundle, 'fragment-based assignments should be reconsidered when fuller structures become available', correction not evolutionary switch, correct level semantics and transfer caveats, automated-match/3c98 note. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. States convergent recruitment across lineages and divergence within homologous superfamily; caveats that separate SCOPe placements do not prove independent origin. Correct level semantics (family/superfamily imply ancestry, fold/class do not). Evidence integration: domain-wide sequence/profile, topology, residue correspondence, evolutionary consistency, biochemical data for function. Rejects function/template transfer. Classifications c.2.1 (51735, fold c.2, class c) and d.58.20.1/d.58.20 (55035)/d.58/class d verified in bundle. Both must_avoid items avoided.

Full before/after comparison with correct SCCS codes, SUNIDs, and the 1dlc A:500-644 boundary, plus the 2.08 reassignment of ColG to b.18.1.36 alongside Cry3A in b.18.1.3. Adds three evidence types: jelly-roll topology, the PubMed 17977833 family comment naming d2quoa_, d1w99a3, and d1nqdb_, and FATCAT statistics for the cluster representative 1nqjA against d2quoa_ at 2.49 angstroms and P of 1.4e-6, correctly attributed to the representative rather than 1nqd and noting that 1nqdA itself returned no stored hits. Rejects collagenolytic, insecticidal, receptor, and galactose transfer and the name-based inference.

All criteria met: family a.4.1.1 supports common ancestry; hf flags structural heterogeneity not rejection of homology, with the inherited a.4 label noted as no guarantee of exemplar topology; template selection requires sequence/mutation, coverage, topology, quality, and complex context checks; geometry and DNA-binding specificity not transferable; datasets retain hf exception and avoid leakage. Identifiers including class 46456 and fold 46688 match the bundle; release 2.08 confirmed via /releases/current. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct on all axes: fragment is incomplete evidence for a retained family member; coverage-aware alignment with missing regions as missing data; d1uc6a1 better initial representative pending checks, fragment retained for local use; diversity compared over shared coverage. SUNIDs, boundaries, hierarchy and fr text correct. Recommends a 'well-resolved' member without any SPACI/AEROSPACI, method or resolution values. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. All must_include items covered with correct hierarchy semantics; explicitly says lack of sequence similarity alone does not justify a new fold and new superfamily does not prove convergence. Frames placements as revisable hypotheses requiring boundary, alignment, profile and conserved-feature evaluation. Example of c.1.1 and c.1.2 as distinct superfamilies within c.1 (SUNID 51350) is directly supported by the children and sccs endpoints in the bundle. No must_avoid violations.

Correct family, superfamily, fold and class identifiers with SUNIDs, all bundle-supported. Superfamily homology vs fold topology vs class correctly separated; family as closer grouping noted without guaranteeing function. Two-lobed catalytic architecture and metal-assisted phosphoryl transfer presented as broad shared principles, not residue-level identity or guaranteed activity. Explicitly bars transfer of protein-substrate recognition, aminoglycoside specificity/resistance, lipid preference, and of activation-loop, autoinhibition, PI3K regulatory-subunit control to APHs. Evidence requirements complete: sequence/profile, phylogeny, catalytic residues and specificity loops, ligand-bound structures, mutational and biochemical data, full-protein architecture, partners, localization, cellular studies. Notes SCOPe does not supply the biochemical evidence. No errors.
